implementation: macOS now uses the Data Protection Keychain. On the original legacy Keychain path, flutter_secure_storage blocked inside SecItemCopyMatching while Security.framework waited in CSSM_DecryptDataFinal. With the Data Protection Keychain, the same read completed and startup reached the signed-out flow.

checks.name: Original macOS startup failure reproduced
checks.observation: The debug app stayed on ‘Подключаемся к гильдии…’. Temporary startup markers localized the wait to FlutterSecureStorage.read.

checks.name: Native Keychain call root cause
checks.observation: The flutter_secure_storage_service serial queue was blocked in SecItemCopyMatching → Security::KeychainCore::ItemImpl::getContent → CSSM_DecryptDataFinal → SecurityServer mach_msg. The login keychain was reported unlocked with no timeout.

checks.name: Data Protection Keychain control run
checks.observation: With usesDataProtectionKeychain enabled, preference and Keychain reads completed, /auth/session returned HTTP 200, and the app displayed the signed-out login screen. This control run used SharedPreferencesAsync to isolate the Keychain setting.

checks.name: Final Keychain setting with existing SharedPreferences API
checks.observation: Restoring the existing SharedPreferences API still completed initialization; the Data Protection Keychain read completed, /auth/session returned HTTP 200, and currentSession finished. The Mac was locked before a second visual capture.

checks.name: macOS release build
checks.observation: The current source rebuilt successfully via `flutter run -d macos --release` as an 84.7 MB app; the runner launched its process without an immediate crash. The resulting app is ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed.

checks.name: Signed macOS release startup and login screen
checks.command: security find-identity -v -p codesigning; inspect app UI after release launch
checks.observation: This host has zero valid code-signing identities and was locked, so the UI could not be inspected. CUA reported that the Mac must be unlocked manually; no unlock or account login was attempted.

remaining: Unlock the Mac and provide a valid Apple Developer signing identity, then run the signed macOS release, verify Keychain write/read persistence across app restart, and confirm the expected re-login behavior for sessions previously stored in the legacy Keychain. The latest ad-hoc launch only proves that the process stayed alive briefly, not that the login UI loaded.
